clue.text: Home to urgent work for one's speech, naturally

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to get home for some urgent work, oddly tied to how one talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges HOME TO URGENT, all twelve letters, into the answer; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The language a person learns first from infancy is the one they speak without effort.

clue.text: Academic cap seen on academic sage

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece seen on another sits above it

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree
a cap is a kind of hat
MA again, the Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A scholar's mortarboard perched on a learned wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'seen on' puts HAT above the second MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahatma is a revered wise person in India, a title of great spiritual standing.

clue.text: What a revolting man, some may say

definitions.text: What a revolting man, some may say

parts.words: What a revolting man, some may say
parts.note: 'What' spoken aloud is the name Wat, so the clue reads as a description of the leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming in disgust at an unpleasant man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting: Wat Tyler led England's Peasants' Revolt in 1381, and 'some may say' turns 'What' into the name Wat.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebel commander of the 1381 uprising in England bore this surname.

clue.text: High-class sort of story

definitions.meaning: upmarket, select, for a privileged few
a news scoop carried by only one paper

explanation.definitionFit: The word means select or upmarket, and also names a news scoop one paper alone carries.

clue.text: Lots of Greeks fought at this sort of weight

definitions.text: Lots of Greeks fought at this
definitions.meaning: the city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad
a system of weights for precious metals

explanation.definitionFit: The ancient city of the Trojan War, and also the weight system jewellers use for gold and silver.

clue.text: Note tricky man executed — he wouldn't swear allegiance

indicators.note: to execute is to behead, so the word loses its head letter

parts.note: a conjuror is a man who does tricks

explanation.surface: A message about a con man being put to death for refusing an oath of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonjurors were clergy who refused the oath of allegiance to William and Mary after 1688; 'executed' here means beheaded, not carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical term for a clergyman who refused to take the loyalty oath to the new monarchs.

clue.text: He taught two pronouns

parts.note: us is a pronoun
her is a second pronoun

explanation.surface: A teacher's grammar lesson on pronouns.
explanation.walkthrough: An usher was once an assistant schoolmaster, an old sense now rare.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English an under-master at a school was called by this name.

clue.text: Boy undercooks animal

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece under another sits below it

parts.note: fries means cooks in a pan
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad who undercooks his food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercooks' must be read as two words, 'under cooks': in a down answer the boy's name sits beneath the word for cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a breed of black-and-white dairy cattle.

clue.text: Raise money in preparation for junket

indicators.note: in a down answer raising a word means reading it upwards, so it is turned backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Collecting funds to pay for a jolly outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junket' looks like a trip, but it is the milk pudding set with rennet. TENNER is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Junket is a sweet curdled-milk pudding, and rennet is the enzyme that curdles it.

clue.text: Queen Mary's share of the money?

definitions.text: Queen Mary's share of the money?

parts.words: Queen Mary's share of the money?
parts.note: Mary II reigned jointly with William III, so her portion of the royal headgear was one of two; the money is a pre-decimal coin

explanation.surface: A question about how much cash a queen received.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-crown was an old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; Mary II shared the throne with William III.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint monarch held one of two shares of royal power, and the coin bore that name.

clue.text: Heroin stuffed right inside socks

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, here within the word for socks

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler hiding narcotics in footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' just colours the picture; 'inside' puts R within HOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is a slang name for the drug in street talk.

clue.text: Bones reveal home of apostle

definitions.meaning: a group of small bones in the ankle
St Paul was born in a city of that name in Asia Minor

explanation.surface: Remains discovered at the birthplace of a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the ankle bones and also the city where St Paul was born.

clue.text: Cut up new loaf

parts.note: to quarter is to cut up into four pieces

explanation.surface: Slicing a fresh loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: A quartern loaf is an old British loaf made with a quarter-stone of flour.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartern is a four-pound loaf, named for the quarter-stone of flour used to make it.

clue.text: Rice is among the starchier grains .

indicators.note: the letters sought are among those of the next word, sitting within it

explanation.surface: A remark that rice is one of the more starchy cereals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice' is a surname: Archie Rice is the fading music-hall comic in John Osborne's play The Entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Osborne's washed-up entertainer has this first name and the surname Rice.

clue.text: Comforts only accepted by prisoners

indicators.note: one word taken in by another, held inside it

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
sole means only

explanation.surface: Inmates who alone receive kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: To console is to soothe someone in distress.

clue.text: But he could have interests other than birds

definitions.text: But he could have interests other than birds

parts.words: But he could have interests other than birds
parts.note: the hobby is a small falcon, so a man whose pastime is that bird might seem limited to it, yet his pastimes can be anything

explanation.surface: A remark that a keen pastime-lover need not be a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The hobby is a small European falcon, so the clue plays on reading the word as 'one devoted to hobbies (the birds)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pursues pastimes for pleasure, with a nod to the falcon called a hobby.

clue.text: Part of head to shampoo and apply conditioning

parts.note: the brain is part of the head
to shampoo is to wash

explanation.surface: A haircare routine: shampoo, then conditioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conditioning' is not hair conditioner but mental conditioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash is to indoctrinate someone by systematic mental pressure.

clue.text: Agree to dissolve a convent

indicators.note: dissolving breaks something up, so these letters are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: Consenting to the closure of a nunnery, as at the Dissolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To covenant is to bind oneself by a formal agreement.

clue.text: Game in Africa badly bent, but bets taken about it

indicators.note: the word for bets goes round the scrambled letters

parts.note: a bookmaker's book is the record of bets taken

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gambler rues a crooked game in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' means wild animals hunted, not a contest, and 'it' in 'about it' points back to the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The bontebok is a South African antelope, a hunted wild animal.

clue.text: Old fool is at the front of the carriage

definitions.text: at the front of the carriage
definitions.meaning: the sprung pad on a railway carriage's end that absorbs impact

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a silly old man, and the shock-absorbing pad on a railway vehicle's end.

clue.text: Great composer suppressed gem

indicators.note: held down inside, so one piece is kept within another

parts.note: Gt is the abbreviation for great, as in Gt Britain
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A celebrated musician kept a jewel hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnet is a red semi-precious stone.

clue.text: To horse! It's over a mile to Sevenoaks, for example

indicators.note: in a down answer pieces over another sit above it

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
M is short for mile

explanation.surface: A rider's cry before a gallop to a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevenoaks is a town in Kent, and its name is a place-name.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is a place-name, and Sevenoaks is one.

clue.text: Fish will sink to the bottom, having swallowed line

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: a ship that founders sinks

explanation.surface: A fish swallows a fishing line and sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is a flatfish.

clue.text: A narrow pass for Nick, say

definitions.meaning: in American usage, a narrow gap between mountains

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a mountain defile in America, and a small V-shaped cut.

clue.text: Take us from Germany to Polish frontier free from obstruction

parts.note: uns is the German word for us

indicators.note: a frontier is a border, so the word's edge letter is taken

explanation.surface: Travel instructions for a trip from Germany to the Polish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Germany' asks for the German word, UNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstop is to clear something blocked, removing what stops it.

clue.text: Chasing game I found inside a stretch of forest

indicators.note: one piece is located inside another

parts.note: tag is the children's chasing game

explanation.surface: Playing chase in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest belt of the sub-Arctic.

clue.text: Depressed by this type of clue?

definitions.meaning: the clue sits in the vertical half of the list

explanation.definitionFit: The word means dejected and also names the vertical clues in a crossword.

clue.text: Books available on previous night for issue

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: eve is the evening before an occasion
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Library books ready the night before a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue in the sense of an outcome is the result of what happens.

clue.text: Love notice given to speech

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A declaration of love announced in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship.

clue.text: Philip said to have sustained flesh wound

definitions.meaning: spoken, the name sounds like fillip, a boost
an injection pierces the upper limb's flesh

explanation.walkthrough: 'Philip said' sounds like 'fillip', a boost or stimulus, which a jab in the upper limb also means figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a boost, like a fillip, and literally a jab into the upper limb.
